shared_elements: low-relief carving on a tall upright stone monolith
repeated row of similar units across a horizontal band
justification: Both surfaces are tall standing slabs carved in low relief with vertically stacked bands, and both include a horizontal row of repeated similar units near the top, which is the most specific shared trait. But A is filled with dense, blocky, abstract glyph-like cartouches in paired columns, while B shows recognisable animals — a row of arched quadrupeds, a crouching predator, a long-legged bird, a scorpion-like creature — plus a fringe/net band, so the actual subject matter is almost entirely different.
